comment: AI 642 phase 1: image points picked on gridded crops (2026-10-12). Pixel coordinates in the original images. b8.png = the target (1122 x 1402); aerial-unannotated.png = supplementary (1122 x 1402).

scale.front_setback_comment: how far the measured centre-bay bands sit behind the front corner's balcony edge. b8 decides it: with 45-degree chamfers the solve only closes at about 1.55 m (0 drives the chamfer to the search bound; sweep 2026-10-13), so the centre bay is recessed by one balcony depth
scale.comment: storey height from the spec (b8's own centre bay then reads 5.3 m against the spec's 5.5 m); balcony projection = the uniform depth the user asked for; the plan's front (balcony edge / podium line) placed at y = -11 like the game podium

where.horizon_heads_y: pedestrians' heads at every distance (eye-height camera)
where.front_band_bottoms_y: bottom edges of the floor slab bands in the front centre bay, floors 5..2 (brightness profile, x 500-620)
where.front_piers_x: the two full-height front piers, outer edges
where.front_corner_x: intersection of the front band line with the right chamfer band line (balcony edge, sharp corner)
where.corner_tangent_px: the front band runs level to x 727, then curves (tangent length on the front)
where.right_chamfer_lines: guard top rails of the deep outer bay on the right chamfer (4 floors) and the band just past the corner
where.far_end_x: the outer bay's slab end at the chamfer-to-side corner
where.podium_top_y: top of the podium, where the first residential floor's guard stands
where.upper_podium_floor_y: band between the ground storefronts and the upper podium (rough)

where.front_left/right: sharp corners of the roof slab's front edge with the front chamfers (the front edge runs y 600-605 between the piers)
where.chamfer_end_left/right: the front chamfers' outer ends, where the roof edge rounds onto the sides
where.side edges: the roof guard beyond those corners, followed back until planters or the penthouse annex hide it

notes: b8 and the aerial are AI-generated images: their perspective is only approximately consistent; numbers carry roughly +/-5-10 % uncertainty.
The rear is visible in neither reference: the rear outline is a design choice.
